title: When a Weather Station Changes Its Address
transcript:
A weather station that has recorded local conditions for decades is being moved to make room for a new road. The new site is only a short distance away, but scientists responsible for the records are treating the relocation as more than a routine delivery of equipment. A small change in surroundings can affect what an instrument measures.

At the original site, the temperature sensor stood near a mature hedge. The proposed location is more open and lies above a surface that dries quickly after rain. Both places can provide useful observations, but their readings may differ even when the wider weather is the same. Joining the two records without noting the move could make a change in measurement conditions resemble a change in climate.

To understand the difference, the team is operating instruments at both locations for an overlapping period. Staff compare readings in sunshine, rain and different wind conditions. They are also recording details of the sites, including the height of nearby vegetation and the position of buildings. These notes will remain with the data after the older station is removed.

The project scientist warns that there may not be a single adjustment that works in every season. A hedge can affect wind and shade differently through the year, and unusual weather may reveal a difference not apparent during ordinary days. The overlap therefore provides evidence about uncertainty rather than a perfect formula for removing it.

For residents following the town's long weather record, the relocation will be clearly marked in the published data. The aim is to keep future users informed about how observations were made. Protecting a record involves preserving that context as well as preserving the numbers themselves.

questions.prompt: Why is the nearby relocation important to the scientists?
options: The instruments can measure temperature only at the original address.
The road will prevent the town from experiencing rain.
Different surroundings may alter the measurements.
The station’s records are too old to be used again.
questions.answer: Different surroundings may alter the measurements.
questions.explanation: 即使只移动很短距离，植被、地表和暴露条件变化也会影响观测。

questions.prompt: What problem could arise if the two records were joined without noting the move?
options: A change in measurement conditions could be mistaken for climate change.
All the earlier numbers would become impossible to read.
The instruments would stop operating during sunshine.
The new road would appear in every temperature graph.
questions.answer: A change in measurement conditions could be mistaken for climate change.
questions.explanation: 站点条件变化造成的差异可能被误判为气候本身发生变化。

questions.prompt: Why are both sites operating during an overlapping period?
options: To double the number of roads included in the project.
To compare their readings under a range of weather conditions.
To avoid recording any information about vegetation.
To allow the old site to be removed immediately.
questions.answer: To compare their readings under a range of weather conditions.
questions.explanation: 同期运行便于在不同天气下比较读数差异，估计迁移影响。

questions.prompt: What limitation of the comparison does the scientist acknowledge?
options: Only one instrument can record wind at a time.
No information about buildings can be preserved.
Published data cannot indicate the date of relocation.
One adjustment may not account for every season and condition.
questions.answer: One adjustment may not account for every season and condition.
questions.explanation: 植被影响随季节和特殊天气变化，不能保证用单一修正公式完全消除差异。
